% Conventional modality balance vs a typed correlation loss vs effective-rank ranking.
% Table~\ref{tab:typed-aux-losses} is auto-generated.

\paragraph{Balance is conventional; it is the wrong symmetric target.}
Write $L_m=\mathrm{CE}(X^{(m)}W_m,Y)$ for a unimodal head.
The usual multimodal balance regularizers are variants of
\begin{equation}
  L_{\mathrm{bal}}
  =
  \sum_m (L_m-\bar L)^2
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  w_m
  =
  \mathrm{softmax}(L_m/\tau),\quad
  L=\sum_m w_m L_m.
\end{equation}
OGM-GE is the same idea on gradient energy $\|X^{(m)\top}(P-e_Y)\|_F$ instead of CE.
All of these are \emph{symmetric}: the lagging head is the one that should receive the next unit of capacity.
That is the correct instinct for a static fusion problem in which every modality is supposed to contribute.
It is the wrong sign for typed shift.
On a covariate hop the visual CE rises because $P(X^{(v)}\mid W)$ moved, not because $P(Y\mid X^{(v)})$ is now more informative; inverse-CE then \emph{raises} $\eta_v$ (Polyak$_m$ by another name).
On clip-level text, $L_t$ is high because the caption does not see $W$; inverse-CE up-weights the structural null.
TSS already refuses that map: large $\hat c_m$ lowers $\eta_m$, both-quiet holds last $\eta_m$.

\paragraph{Correlation: do not invent a third intensity; redesign the off-diagonal.}
Let $z_i^{(m)}$ be the coordinate-mean of block $m$ (the same scalar used for $\hat c_m$).
Point-biserial $\mathrm{Corr}(z^{(m)},W)$ is Cohen's $d$ in correlation units; it must not be sold as a new channel.
The object that is \emph{not} already in TSS is the cross-modal Gram $C_{mm'}=\mathrm{Corr}(z^{(m)},z^{(m')})$ on the pooled pair of batches.
An unweighted Barlow / CCA / CLIP pair-loss maximizes every $C_{mm'}$.
That lets a moving visual mean drag a quiet caption head into encoding $W$.
The typed replacement weights the off-diagonal by the covariate intensities already estimated,
\begin{equation}
  L_{\mathrm{corr}}
  =
  \sum_{m\neq m'}
  \hat c_m
  \Bigl(1-\frac{\hat c_{m'}}{\sum_{k}\hat c_k}\Bigr)
  C_{mm'}^{2}.
\end{equation}
A moving head pays for correlating with a quiet head; two concept-active heads are not penalized; two quiet heads stay off (hold).
This is an EWC-style representation penalty on the same $(\hat c,\hat\delta)$ pair, not a second product loop and not $\eta\propto\pi$.
On the recorded covariate hop $L_{\mathrm{corr}}=0.491$ (the video${}\to{}$audio leak dominates); on the concept hop it is $0.004$ because $\hat c$ is quiet.

\paragraph{Effective rank is a ranking, not a loss type.}
Roy--Vetterli
$\mathrm{erank}(A)=\exp H(\tilde\sigma)$
turns a spectrum into a scalar between $1$ and $\mathrm{rank}(A)$.
It does \emph{not} sit next to $(\hat c,\hat\delta)$ as a third intensity.

Three places people reach for it, and only one of them is new.

\emph{(i)~$\mathrm{erank}(\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}} X^{(m)})$ and $\Delta\mathrm{erank}_m$.}
Centered covariance is location-invariant: $X\mapsto X+a1^{\top}$ does not change the spectrum.
The oracle covariate hop is exactly that location shift (an all-ones drift on the block).
$\Delta\mathrm{erank}(\mathrm{Cov})$ is then sampling noise, and on the recorded pair it ranks text $>$ audio $>$ video --- the opposite of $\hat c$.
A concept hop that only permutes $P(Y\mid X)$ inside a balanced mixture does not change $\mathrm{Cov}\,X$ either.
Do not read $\Delta\mathrm{erank}(\mathrm{Cov})$ as the covariate sign.

\emph{(ii)~erank of a $2\times 2$ cosine Gram of consecutive batch means.}
Eigenvalues of
$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&\rho\\ \rho&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
are $1\pm\rho$, so $\mathrm{erank}$ is a monotone function of $|\rho|$.
Ranking hops by that scalar is ranking hops by $1-\cos(\bar x_{t-1},\bar x_t)$, already the Amazon heatmap $\hat c$.
On the oracle DGP consecutive drifted means stay collinear, cosine stays near $1$, and this ranking does \emph{not} put video first.
The $2\times 2$ Gram is a shared language with the heatmap, not a new hop score.

\emph{(iii)~$\mathrm{erank}(R)$ of the $K\times K$ cosine$(B_i,B_j)$ Gram, with leave-one-out $\Delta\mathrm{erank}$.}
This is the ranking that is not already $\hat c$.
$R$ is one kernel, not a hop.
$\mathrm{erank}(R)$ says how many independent domains the stream has ($2.74$ of $K=9$ on Amazon).
Leave-one-out $\Delta\mathrm{erank}$ ranks which category is the extra direction: Gift Cards and Subscription Boxes collapse the spectrum; Music / Mag / Beauty barely move it.
That order agrees with the two large $1-\cos$ hops (Gift$\to$Music, Software$\to$SubBox) without being a rewrite of a single hop.
Use it to order which domain the existing $(\hat c,\hat\delta)$ map is allowed to touch.
Do not add $\mathrm{erank}$ as a third intensity.

% Conventional modality balance vs a typed correlation loss vs effective-rank ranking.
% Table~\ref{tab:typed-aux-losses} is identification. Table~\ref{tab:typed-aux-risk} is the risk layer.

\paragraph{How this is evaluated.}
The object is a \emph{typed} multimodal regularizer, not a new VQA number.
Evaluation is therefore two-layer, and the layers are not interchangeable.

\emph{Layer 1 --- identification, pre-specified.}
On an oracle hop whose type is known, does the regularizer fire on the right head and stay off on the wrong hop?
Covariate-only (video mean drift, clip-level text a structural null) and concept-only (video label-map rotation, $P(X)$ fixed) are the two probes.
The claims are signed:
inverse-CE / OGM-GE must \emph{not} match $\hat c$ on a covariate hop (it is allowed to put text first);
$\mathrm{Corr}(z^{(m)},W)$ must match $\hat c$ (it is the same intensity);
typed $L_{\mathrm{corr}}$ must be large on covariate and near zero on concept;
$\Delta\mathrm{erank}(\mathrm{Cov})$ must \emph{fail} to rank the mean hop (location-invariant);
leave-one-out $\Delta\mathrm{erank}(R)$ on the Amazon cosine Gram must rank Gift Cards and Subscription Boxes with the $1-\cos$ hops.
Table~\ref{tab:typed-aux-losses} is this layer.
A regularizer that cannot type the hop is not entered into the risk comparison as a typed method --- it is a conventional blender.

\emph{Layer 2 --- risk, also pre-specified, not a leaderboard.}
If the hop is typed, does the step move the metric that hop is supposed to move?
Covariate-only: backward transfer (accuracy and Brier on batch~0 after the stream) --- do not chase $X$.
Concept-only: post-change accuracy / CE --- relearn $P(Y\mid X)$.
Amazon 9-category rating stream: online MSE and BWT MSE, with plateau as the clock that already won that board.
Brier $\mathbb{E}\|P-e_Y\|_2^2$ is the MSE of the multimodal probe; Amazon is scalar rating MSE.
Do not pool them into one ``multimodal score'': a method that helps concept post-change by chasing $X$ is a failure on the covariate hop.
Table~\ref{tab:typed-aux-risk} is this layer.
Balance is allowed to \emph{hurt} BWT. Typed $L_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is an EWC-style leak penalty, not a joint-CE minimizer, so a small online-MSE cost is acceptable if BWT holds. Hop-Gram erank extra-shrink is stronger TSS, not a third intensity; it should not be sold as a new win if plateau still has lower Amazon MSE.

No ImageNet-scale fusion claim. MSR-VTT windows remain an illustration of $\hat c$ and the quiet-text hold.

\paragraph{Why this is a promising multimodal-learning direction.}
Static multimodal learning has two mature poles, and typed shift sits in the gap between them.

The first pole is \emph{modality competition / imbalance}.
Gradient blending, OGM-GE, PMR, QMF, and MMPareto all treat a lagging unimodal CE (or gradient energy) as a bug: the next unit of capacity should go to the weak head so that fusion uses every modality.
That is the right instinct on an i.i.d.\ fusion problem in which every block is supposed to contribute.
It is the wrong map once $W$ indexes a domain hop.
A visual CE rise can be $P(X^{(v)}\mid W)$ moving while $P(Y\mid X^{(v)})$ is still valid; inverse-CE then raises $\eta_v$ (Polyak$_m$).
Clip-level text has high $L_t$ because the caption does not see $W$; the same blender up-weights the structural null.
The promising move is not another softmax on $L_m$.
It is to \emph{type} the imbalance with $(\hat c_m,\hat\delta_m)$ before choosing a sign: covariate $\Rightarrow$ shrink the moving head; concept $\Rightarrow$ raise it; both quiet $\Rightarrow$ hold.
Conventional balance becomes a signed ablation, not the method.

The second pole is \emph{cross-modal agreement}: CLIP, CCA, Barlow, and pair losses \emph{maximize} $C_{mm'}$.
Under a covariate hop that is leakage: a moving visual mean drags a quiet caption head into encoding $W$.
Typed
$L_{\mathrm{corr}}=\sum_{m\neq m'}\hat c_m(1-\hat c_{m'}/\sum_k\hat c_k)C_{mm'}^{2}$
is the missing opposite sign --- an alignment penalty gated by the same intensities TSS already estimates.
It is closer to EWC on the off-diagonal than to a contrastive objective, which is why it belongs next to the stepsize rather than as a second product loop.

Leave-one-out $\mathrm{erank}(R)$ of the batch-relationship Gram is the dataset diagnostic those two poles usually skip.
Multimodal papers report one number on a mixed test set.
$\mathrm{erank}(R)=2.74$ of $K=9$ says the Amazon stream is a few domains, not nine independent tasks; Gift and SubBox are the extra directions.
Evaluation should stratify by hop, which is Layer 2 above.
Ranking domains is how the existing $(\hat c,\hat\delta)$ map chooses what to touch; it is not a third loss.

\emph{Risk numbers, not oversold.}
On the linear probe the covariate BWT accuracy is at ceiling ($1.0$): a global mean hop does not destroy class means in the first $r$ coordinates, so BWT acc is not the sensitive metric --- online CE / Brier is.
TSS online CE $0.641$ (Brier $0.046$); inv-CE balance $0.653$ / $0.048$ (slightly worse on covariate, slightly better on concept: CE $0.329$ vs $0.362$); typed $L_{\mathrm{corr}}$ on mean-logits matches TSS (the learned heads are already weakly correlated, so the extra gradient is nearly inactive); hop-Gram erank extra-shrink \emph{raises} CE to $0.909$ / $0.640$ because on this DGP the $2\times 2$ Gram ranks the quiet head first.
Amazon rating MSE: plateau $1.597$, TSS $1.631$, TSS$+L_{\mathrm{corr}}$ $1.631$ (no cut), TSS$+$erank $1.651$ online but BWT MSE $0.841$ vs $0.883$ (stronger freeze, the expected trade).
These auxiliaries do not beat plateau on Amazon MSE.
That is not a failure of the direction: Layer 1 already shows conventional balance has the wrong sign, and Layer 2 shows that using erank as a second intensity hurts.
The promising claim is the typed evaluation protocol, not a new lowest MSE.

The numbers, the identification figure, and both tables live in
\texttt{results/typed\_aux\_losses/}.
